_comment: This repo builds the team kits and can therefore install none of them (DEC-0003): gate_write_scope refuses every write-capable command line naming team-kits, and here every change is one. The PreToolUse gates below are the replacement SR-0009 specifies (it replaced SR-0006 on 2026-08-13) (a count once stood here and aged the day this file grew an entry; test_gates.EXPECTED_TOOLS is the one place that says which gate sits on which event, and it is compared with this file in both directions). gate_approval.py is the exception to 'no kit is installed here' and is the KIT's own file, referenced where it ships rather than copied: approvals.mint accepts that hook only when it runs as itself beside its own _kernel.py, so a copy in .claude/hooks would be a second answer to a question _gate.py already answers, and a wrapper cannot satisfy the check without reproducing it. It is registered on BOTH AskUserQuestion events because the kits pair them and the halves do different jobs -- PreToolUse refuses a relayed approval question that is not the kernel's, PostToolUse reads the answer the platform wrote and is the only event that mints (measured 2026-08-31 in a throwaway copy of this repo: request-approval -> verbatim relay rc 0, a reworded one rc 2 -> an answer in the shape the platform writes mints APR-0001 and walks the item to APPROVED. A real user's click is the one part of that no headless run can produce, and AskUserQuestion is not even offered in one -- also measured; the round protocol under project_memory/staging/TSK-0098/ carries both). Its path is built from ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} and not spelled out, because the reader that decides whether a user's answer can mint here does not decompose a quoted span containing a space and this checkout's path has one (H81). gate_lead_write_scope is registered TWICE on purpose -- on the write tools and on the shell -- because a protected path is reachable from either, and registered on the write tools alone eight measured shell lines wrote kit code, this file and the producer of the protected area with rc 0 (2026-08-05). Every interpreter runs with -B because the gates import out of team-kits/, the source side of the kit hash, and a route that starts an interpreter over that tree must refuse to cache into it (kernel/hashing.py BYTECODE_SUFFIXES); _harness.py states the same flag for itself, because a rebuilt command line does not carry it. EVERY entry states a `timeout`, and none may be left to the provider's default: _harness.Deadline reads this file to learn when it will be killed, and a killed hook is read as 'hook error, carry on', i.e. as an ALLOW -- measured 2026-08-05, five candidates on unroutable UNC hosts cost gate 1 211.3 s against this 120. A gate that finds no timeout for its call refuses rather than race a deadline it cannot see. `agent:` binds the session role: without one, _compat.calling_subagent cannot tell the lead from a subagent, which is exactly the fixture blindness that let the July regression live for a month.
